# Quick Study Guide: 3.1 Single Document Insertion (insertOne())

> "insertOne(document) inserts a single document into a collection. If the collection doesn't exist yet, MongoDB creates it automatically."

## 1. Rapid Visual & Core Concept Summary

Executing `db.<collectionName>.insertOne(<document>)` serializes a single JavaScript object into a length-prefixed BSON byte buffer, injects a deterministic 12-byte `ObjectId` (`_id`) if omitted by the caller, and dispatches an `{ insert: "<col>", documents: [ <doc> ] }` wire command to `mongod`.

The architectural diagram above illustrates single-document BSON serialization during `insertOne()`: polymorphic type tagging (`0x02` UTF-8 string, `0x10` int32, `0x04` array), 12-byte `ObjectId` primary key generation, and atomic persistence into WiredTiger. At the storage engine boundary, this sub-topic governs how `mongod` coordinates `OP_MSG` wire frames, WiredTiger `.wt` table and B-tree index extents, and document-level concurrency latches.

## 2. Must-Know Syntax & Mechanics (Top 75% Exam Focus)

- **L-3.1 Command Syntax & BSON Polymorphic Type Serialization.** `insertOne(document, options)` validates that `document` is a non-array object and serializes each attribute with its BSON type byte: UTF-8 string (`0x02`), 32/64-bit integer (`0x10`/`0x12`), array (`0x04`), embedded document (`0x03`), boolean (`0x08`), or UTC datetime (`0x09`).
- **L-3.2 12-Byte `ObjectId` Synthesis & Return Telemetry.** Every document requires a unique `_id` indexed in the primary `_id_` B-tree. When omitted, the driver synthesizes a 12-byte (96-bit) `ObjectId` comprising a **4-byte big-endian UNIX epoch timestamp**, a **5-byte process/machine random value**, and a **3-byte big-endian incrementing counter**, returning `{ acknowledged: true, insertedId: ObjectId("...") }`.

```javascript
// Single-document BSON ingestion with automatic 12-byte ObjectId synthesis
const res = db.students.insertOne({
  name: "Rahul",
  age: 19,
  grade: 9,
  subjects: ["Math", "Science"]
});
// res -> { acknowledged: true, insertedId: ObjectId("6544b102c9e77c0012a40001") }
// Extract embedded creation timestamp from the first 4 bytes of ObjectId:
res.insertedId.getTimestamp();
```

## 3. Rapid Revision Flowchart & Cheat-Sheet Table

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["JS Object { name, age, subjects }"] --> B["Driver BSON Serializer"]
    B --> C["Inject 12B ObjectId (4B Time | 5B Rand | 3B Ctr)"]
    C --> D["OP_MSG { insert: 'students', documents: [doc] }"]
    D --> E["WiredTiger Table + _id_ B-Tree Commit"]
```

| 12-Byte `ObjectId` Segment | Byte Offset & Width | Encoding & Architectural Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Epoch Timestamp | Bytes `0–3` (`4` bytes / 32 bits) | Big-endian seconds since UNIX epoch (rough creation sort order) |
| Random Value | Bytes `4–8` (`5` bytes / 40 bits) | Random value unique to the client machine and process |
| Incrementing Counter | Bytes `9–11` (`3` bytes / 24 bits) | Big-endian counter initialized to a random seed (prevents same-second collisions) |

## 4. High-Yield Exam Traps

- **Exam Trap — 12-Byte `ObjectId` Breakdown**: Memorize the `4 + 5 + 3 = 12` byte structure of `ObjectId` (`4B` timestamp, `5B` random value, `3B` incrementing counter = 24 hex characters).
- **Immutability of `_id`**: Once a document is inserted via `insertOne()`, its `_id` field is strictly immutable and can never be modified by `$set`.
- **BSON Size Limit**: A single BSON document inserted via `insertOne()` cannot exceed the `16 MB` (`16,777,216` bytes) maximum BSON document size limit.
